sentences.text: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 10.05.2022 at about 4.30 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding in motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-40-U-1131 near Yalloda, Adinarayanaswamy Hills,
Gudibande Taluk, Chikkaballapura, at that time, driver of Auto bearing registration No.AP-39-TX-8988 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to impact, petitioner sustained injuries all over the body.

3. It is further stated that, immediately the petitioner was shifted to Chikkaballapura Government Hospital, after first aid treatment he was shifted to Prolife Multi Speciality Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines, conveyance etc.,
4.

It is stated that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 24 years and working as farmer and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m. Due to accidental injuries, he could not able to do his work as earlier.
5. It is stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of the Auto bearing registration No.AP-39-TX-8988.
Hence, the jurisdictional Gudibande Traffic police have registered a criminal case against driver of said vehicle in Cr.No.81/2022.
As such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
6. After service of summons, respondent No.1 & 2 have appeared through their respective counsel & respondent No.2 filed the written statement.
Inspite of giving sufficient time, the respondent No.1 has not filed his written statement.

7. The respondent No.2 filed the written statement and admitted about the issuance of policy in respect of Auto bearing registration No.AP-39-TX-8988 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It is contended that, the driver of offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
It is the defence of the respondent No.2 that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner and not on the part of the driver of the Auto.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Ultimately contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

Such statement cannot be relied upon as it has no evidentiary value".

. On watching the video it appears that, the person stating that Adinarayana was driving the vehicle.

By applying the principle laid down in the supra decision, it can be held that, there is no evidentiary value to Ex.R7 in the absence of the examination of author of the CD.
22.

In the light of the discussion held above, it is crystal clear that, the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of the Auto bearing registration No.AP-39-TX-8988.
As such, the petitioner has placed the satisfactory and convincing evidence on record to prove the above issue.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
23.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

24. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injuries cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of Chandrashaker vs U. Adinarayana on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42951173/

PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P.6.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Right lateral wall orbit fracture,
2) Contusion right frontal region 3) CLW over right hand, right foot, paristal region of head 4) CLW over lower to be of right ear, over right eyebrow 5) Righ mid foot avulsion injury with skin loss 26.
In connection with the above said injuries the doctor is of the opinion that, the said injuries are grievous in nature.

Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summary issued by Prolife Multi Speciality Hospital as per Ex.P10, which reveals that petitioner was admitted to the said Hospital from 10.05.2022 to 17.05.2022.
Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of MRO of Prolife Multispeciality Hospital as PW2.

case sheet and x-ray at per Ex.P17 to Ex.P21.

He has deposed that the petitioner has sustained right proximal humerus, open fracture 3rd Metacarpal Head, Compound Type III C dislocation of all joints of right foot and deloving injury of right foot.

He has placed inpatient record and x-ray as per Ex.P22 &
Ex.P23.

On going through the discharge summary and mode of treatment given to him as fully narrated in the recitals of the above documents and the recitals of the case files of the petitioner,
clearly evident that, the petitioner could have suffered a lot of pain and sufferings, due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident. By taking into consideration of all these points, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.50,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

On perusal of discharge summary marked at Ex.P10 issued by Prolife Hospitals, which discloses that he was admitted from 10.05.2022 and discharged on 17.05.2022.

During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to his to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a Chandrashaker vs U. Adinarayana on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42951173/

The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses, he has produced medical bills at Ex.P13 to the extent of Rs.4,88,948/- along with prescriptions at Ex.P13.
Except the suguestion there are no contra materials available on record to disprove the medical bills.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
29.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summary the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as attendant charges.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,000/- towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
30.
The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P6 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injuries for which he took the treatment as an inpatient.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.S.A.Somashekara. examined as PW3.

He has stated in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained right proximal humerus, opend #3rd Metacarpal Head, Compound Type III C dislocation of all joints of right foot and deloving injury of right foot, for which he underwent ORIF withPHILOS for fracture proximal humerus, wound debridement adn K-wire fixation and wound closure and wound debridement and K-wire fixation of right foot under GA.

In support of his evidence he has produced clinical notes and x-ray at Ex.P22 & Ex.P23.
31.

Further, PW3 has stated that, at the time of examination of the petitioner, he wals with pain and limping wasting of right sided limbs, surgical scars are seen over right shoulder x-rays shows united fracture proximal humerus right with PHILOS plate in situ, malunited fracture head of 3rd MC and 3rd proximal phalanx right hand., aligned mid tarsal joints right foot.
he has assessed permanent physical disability of both right upper limb and right lower limb at 65% and whole body disability is at 33%.

sentences.text: Over all appreciation of evidence of PW3 along with the entire medical documents the whole body disability expressed by PW3 as physical disability for limb is 65% and whole body is 33%.
Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW3, it is apt to take whole body disability as 18% instead of 33%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.
33. In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 24 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed any Aadhar card at Ex.P15 for consideration.
On perusal of the said document, his date of birth is mentioned as 01.01.1998.
The alleged accident occurred on 10.05.2022.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 24 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '18' is to be taken into consideration.

34. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident he was working as farmer and getting an income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not placed any iota of documents.
In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2022.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,500/- for the year 2022.
35. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner

,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,500 X12 X 18 X 18/100= Rs.6,02,640/-.
Loss of amenities;
36.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries, he is unable to walk, stand long time, limping while walking, not able to sit cross leg and not able to use Indian toilet.

On perusal of evidence of PW1 and PW3 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.25,000/- towards loss of amenities.

Future Medical Expenses;
37.
PW3 has stated that petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants, which would cost around Rs.30,000/-.
Either PW1 or PW3 have not placed any estimation in this regard.

On going through the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also escalation of rates in the medical field, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of future medication.

LIABILITY:
40.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Auto bearing registration No.AP-39-TX-8988 alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.
41. The respondent No.2 had contended in its written statement that the offending vehicle had no valid permit as on the date of accident.
In this regard the respondent No.2 has examined Official of the RTO, Hindupura, Andhrapradesh as RW1.
He has placed authorisation letter and permit at Ex.R1 & Ex.R2.
42. Further examined its Legal Manager as RW2.
He has deposed in his evidence that autorickshaw bearing No.AP-39-TX-8988 is having permit "within the radius of 60 Kms from the residence of the owner, expect prohibited routes".
Further stated that the alleged accident taken place Near "Yallodu Adinarayanaswami Hills, Gudibande Taluk, Chickballapur District, Karnataka within the limits of Budibande police limits.
Hence, there is no permit to the autorickshaw bearing No.AP-39-TX-8988 as on the date of accident.

43. At this stage, it is relevant to rely the decision reported in 2018 ACJ 2430 between Rani and Others Vs. National Insurance Company Limited and others, Wherein it is held that, "in connection with the permit came to the conclusion to direct the insurance company to deposit the amount of compensation with liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle."

sentences.text: 44. In the light of the supra decision, I am of the view that, in the present case also there was no valid permit as on the date of the accident.
Same point has been clearly bringforth to the evidence of RW1 and the documentary evidence Ex.
R2 . Though insurance policy pertaining to the offending vehicle was in force due to non-availability of the permit in the present case also principle of pay and recovery has to be followed.

Accordingly, the respondent No.2, being the insurance company has to pay the compensation amount determined by this court with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization, with a liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle i.e., from the respondent No.1 through due process of law.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
45.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.12,25,588/- (Rupees twelve lakhs twenty five thousand five hundred and eighty eight only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The respondent No.2 being the insurance company, is liable to pay the compensation determined by this court, with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order, thereafter, recover the same, from the respondent No.1 the owner of the vehicle.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
It is contended that, the driver of offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident, hence there is a violation of terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
It is the defence of the respondent No.2 that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner and not on the part of the driver of the Auto.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.

opennyai_summary.issue:
On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues;
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident that was taken place on 10.05.2022 at about 4.30 p.m., near Yallodu Adinarayanaswamy Hills,
Gudibande Taluk, Chickkaballapur District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Auto bearing registration No.AP-  39-TX-8988 in an actionable  negligence ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate? from whom?
3. What order or award?

opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
ISSUE No.3:
45.
In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.12,25,588/- (Rupees twelve lakhs twenty five thousand five hundred and eighty eight only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 being the insurance company, is liable to pay the compensation determined by this court, with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order, thereafter, recover the same, from the respondent No.1 the owner of the vehicle.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
